briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The past 24 hours have seen intense direct military exchanges between the United States and Iran, characterized by multiple US airstrikes across Iranian cities and significant Iranian missile and drone retaliations against US bases in the Gulf region and Jordan. This escalation comes amidst fresh intelligence reports of Iran relocating thousands of uranium centrifuges to a fortified underground facility, and a Houthi declaration of a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia, further destabilizing the region.

IRAN
The United States conducted multiple waves of airstrikes against Iran, targeting military command centers, naval capabilities, missile and drone launch sites, and air defense systems in various cities including Shiraz, Bandar Abbas, Chabahar, Konarak, Abdanan, and Khomein. While the Governor of Isfahan denied attacks, residents reported explosions. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and Army retaliated with extensive missile and drone operations. They claimed to have destroyed US early-warning radars, missile defense radar systems (including Patriot and AN/FPS-117), F-15 fighter jets, MQ-9 drones, and satellite communication systems at US bases in Kuwait (Arifjan, Al Udairi, Ahmad Al Jaber), Bahrain (Sheikh Isa, Muharraq, Riffa), and Jordan (Muwaffaq Salti Air Base, Al-Rukban area). The IRGC also claimed to have launched cruise missiles at Amazon's central data infrastructure in Bahrain and accused the US of attacking the Darkhovin Nuclear Power Plant, urging the UN Security Council to condemn it. Air defense systems were reportedly activated near the Bushehr nuclear power plant.

Two oil tankers were reportedly struck and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz or near Oman. The IRGC claimed responsibility for halting two "violating" tankers, blaming the US for misleading vessels, and declared the Strait of Hormuz closed as long as US hostile actions continue. Ali Bagheri-Kani, Deputy Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, asserted that the Strait of Hormuz is "crucial leverage" for Iran.

Israeli intelligence indicates Iran moved thousands of uranium enrichment centrifuges to tunnels deep inside Pickaxe Mountain, near Natanz, following the 12-day war. This development, communicated to the US, is believed to be an effort to reconstitute its nuclear program. Iran denied a Reuters report of a 10-day ceasefire proposal with the US, though senior Iranian officials confirmed that mediators (including Qatar) have presented new proposals for de-escalation which are under consideration. Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni traveled to Pakistan with a message on negotiations. Qalibaf, Iran's Parliament Speaker, accused the US of sending new military equipment while claiming to seek peace, asserting Iran's "full mastery" in recognizing US tactics. Reports of electricity cuts and internet blackouts affecting news flow were noted in various Iranian areas.

ISRAEL
Prime Minister Netanyahu convened an overnight security meeting. Finance Minister Smotrich stated that Israel has no interest in joining the limited US-Iran confrontation, viewing the current situation, including the American naval blockade, as "the most favorable outcome for Israel," with the broader objective being the collapse of Iran's government. He warned Iran would "regret it" if it fired at Israel. Israel has raised its alert levels to the highest point, preparing for a new escalation phase, pending a decision from President Trump.

IDF and Shin Bet operations in Gaza killed Adham Ibrahim Shaaban Nasman, identified as the chief of operations for Hamas's Gaza City Brigade, who directed the October 7 infiltration and held at least seven hostages. Emily Damari, a former hostage, reacted by saying "they are burning in hellfire." The IDF also eliminated Taher Ahmad Salem Abd al-Wahed, a Palestinian Islamic Jihad (PIJ) operative who infiltrated the Nova music festival on October 7 and commanded the abduction of Inbar Haiman, whose remains were returned in October 2025. Another PIJ operative, Salah Subhi Salah Qatrawi, was killed for attempting to advance terror plots near aid distribution sites.

In southern Lebanon, the "Safe Zone" pilot program commenced, with Israeli forces withdrawing from Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh for the first time and Lebanese army units deploying there, as well as in Froun and Srifa. The IDF is coordinating this program with the US military and Lebanese Armed Forces, viewing it as a test of Lebanese Army sovereignty. IDF activities to destroy terror infrastructure in Lebanon resulted in loud explosions in the Upper Galilee. The IDF will conduct a military exercise in the Zikim coast area on July 22.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli military operations resulted in the killing of key Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad (PIJ) operatives in Gaza. Adham Ibrahim Shaaban Nasman, Hamas's chief of operations for the Gaza City Brigade, was killed in Gaza City. Taher Ahmad Salem Abd al-Wahed and Salah Subhi Salah Qatrawi, both PIJ operatives, were killed in central Gaza. An Israeli Air Force (IAF) strike in the Gaza Strip killed six family members, with the IDF stating the target was a Hamas operative and the results are under review. Three individuals were reported killed in a vehicle attack near Khan Yunis hospital. Khalil al-Hayya has been chosen as the new head of Hamas's Political Bureau, replacing Sinwar.

LEBANON
The "Safe Zone" pilot program began with the deployment of Lebanese army units into Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh, Froun, and Srifa, following an initial withdrawal of Israeli forces from Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh. This program involves coordination between the IDF, the US military (CENTCOM), and the Lebanese Armed Forces. Lebanese army engineering teams are scanning streets in Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh for explosives and remnants left by the IDF. While the Lebanese army is committed to clearing Hezbollah weapons, two points remain unresolved: the identity of the supervising entity and the criteria for defining a "clean area." Lebanese President Aoun is expected to seek a commitment from US President Trump for a full Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon, a sentiment echoed by Speaker Nabih Berri. Israeli artillery shelled Nabatieh al-Fawqa in southern Lebanon, and IDF operations to destroy terror infrastructure led to explosions in the Upper Galilee region of Israel.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Pro-Iranian Iraqi militias, led by Nujaba leader Firas al-Alyasar, threatened to join the conflict if operations against Tehran escalate, warning that the US presence is the primary cause of regional tension and stating they would remain in open war with US forces if they do not depart by September. Explosions were reported in Sulaymaniyah, northern Iraq, and a drone was downed near Iraq’s Al-Harir airbase in eastern Erbil.

Jordan intercepted five Iranian drones. Earlier, two US soldiers, Tyler James Feehan (25) and Isabella Gonzales (19), were killed in an Iranian ballistic missile attack on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan on July 17. US officials detailed three separate missile strikes on the base, which hit a gym (wounding some troops), an empty aircraft hangar, and prefabricated housing units where soldiers were sleeping. Satellite imagery shows new impact points at King Faisal Air Base in Jordan. The IRGC claimed to have destroyed a missile-defense radar system and an F-15 fighter jet inside a hangar at a US base in Jordan and attacked a complex housing US military personnel in the al-Rukban area, claiming "several" casualties. Sirens sounded in Jordan following launches from Iran.

GULF STATES
**Saudi Arabia:** The Houthi military spokesperson declared an immediate maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia in retaliation for the Kingdom's alleged blockade and attacks on Yemen. The Saudi Foreign Ministry condemned this declaration, dismissing it as an attempt to divert attention from Houthi economic crises and crimes against Yemenis, reiterating Saudi Arabia's pursuit of peace in Yemen. There was an unconfirmed report of a Saudi tanker being hit by an Iranian missile in the Strait of Hormuz.
**UAE:** The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported an incident 17 nautical miles east of Dibba, UAE, where a vessel was struck by an unknown projectile, damaging its steering gear, though all crew members were safe.
**Kuwait:** Kuwaiti air defense systems were actively intercepting incoming Iranian missiles and drones, with explosions heard. Iranian forces, including the IRGC and Army, claimed extensive attacks on US bases in Kuwait, including Arifjan, Al Udairi, and Ahmad Al Jaber Air Base. Targets included administrative buildings, helicopter parking, troop accommodation, HIMARS missile systems, radar systems, and an MQ-9 drone hangar. The Kuwaiti government reportedly threatened 10 years imprisonment for anyone publishing photos or videos of the attacks. Kuwaiti citizens have called for stopping advertising screens due to power consumption issues following Iranian attacks, indicating potential strain on infrastructure. A Kuwaiti oil tanker was reportedly attacked near Oman.
**Bahrain:** Explosions were heard in Bahrain. Iranian forces claimed to have attacked Sheikh Isa Air Base, Muharraq, and Riffa, destroying a Patriot air defense system and other radar systems. The IRGC also claimed a cruise missile attack on the central data infrastructure of the American company Amazon in Bahrain. A Chinese air defense system was reportedly observed in Bahrain.
**Oman:** The UKMTO reported a maritime incident near Limah, Oman, where a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile, leading the crew to abandon the vessel in lifeboats. This tanker was identified as a Kuwaiti oil tanker.
**Qatar:** Qatari mediators proposed a 10-day cessation of strikes between the US and Iran to explore ways to revive an interim deal, which Iran is examining. Qatar also informed the UN and UN Security Council of an Iranian targeting of the Qatari tanker Al-Rikayat near the Strait of Hormuz on July 7, 2026, and a missile attack on Qatar on July 12, 2026. The US State Department issued a "Global Alert" for American citizens due to "increasing tensions in the Middle East," advising heightened caution and preparedness for travel disruptions. President Trump discussed mine clearing from the Strait of Hormuz with the new UK Prime Minister.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **US Strikes on Iran:** The US launched multiple waves of airstrikes against military command centers, naval capabilities, missile and drone sites, and air defense systems across various Iranian cities, including Shiraz, Bandar Abbas, Chabahar, Konarak, Abdanan, and Khomein.
2.  **Iranian Retaliation:** Iran's IRGC and Army conducted extensive missile and drone attacks targeting US bases in Kuwait (Arifjan, Al Udairi, Ahmad Al Jaber), Bahrain (Sheikh Isa, Muharraq, Riffa), and Jordan (Muwaffaq Salti Air Base, Al-Rukban), claiming destruction of radar systems, F-15 jets, MQ-9 drones, and infliction of casualties.
3.  **US Casualties in Jordan:** Two US soldiers, Tyler James Feehan (25) and Isabella Gonzales (19), were killed on July 17 in an Iranian ballistic missile attack on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan, which struck prefabricated housing units. The Pentagon confirmed nearly 100 US service members were injured in Iranian attacks this month.
4.  **Iran's Nuclear Activity:** Israeli intelligence assesses that Iran moved thousands of uranium enrichment centrifuges to deep tunnels within Pickaxe Mountain (near Natanz) after the 12-day war, signaling efforts to rebuild its nuclear program. This information was shared with the US.
5.  **Strait of Hormuz Incidents:** Two oil tankers were reportedly struck and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz or near Oman. The IRGC claimed responsibility for halting two "violating" tankers and declared the Strait closed if US aggression continues.
6.  **Lebanon "Safe Zone" Pilot:** The "Safe Zone" pilot program began in southern Lebanon with the withdrawal of Israeli forces from Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh and the deployment of Lebanese army units in Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh, Froun, and Srifa, in coordination with the US.
7.  **Houthi Maritime Blockade:** Yemen's Houthi forces declared an immediate maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia, citing the Kingdom's actions in Yemen. Saudi Arabia's Foreign Ministry condemned this as a distraction.
8.  **Hamas Leadership Change:** Khalil al-Hayya was chosen as the new head of Hamas's Political Bureau, replacing Sinwar.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks remain critically high, with direct US-Iran military confrontation underway. The US is conducting strikes deep within Iran, while Iran is retaliating against US military assets across the Gulf and in Jordan, coupled with assertive rhetoric from both sides. Israel's intelligence on Iran's renewed centrifuge activity at Pickaxe Mountain could serve as a significant flashpoint for further US or Israeli action against Iran's nuclear program. Active flashpoints include the Strait of Hormuz, where maritime attacks and Iran's declared control directly challenge US stated objectives for free navigation. Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan are experiencing direct Iranian attacks on US bases. Southern Lebanon is in a delicate phase with Israeli withdrawal and Lebanese army deployment, with concerns over Hezbollah rearmament persisting. The Houthi maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia introduces a new layer of regional instability.

Military posture changes include the deployment of additional US F-16 and F-35 fighter jets and refueling tankers to the Middle East, while the Pentagon is reportedly constrained by dwindling munition stockpiles and potential unsustainability of operations. Iran has escalated its missile and drone capabilities and reportedly mobilized its 65th Army Brigade. Israel has heightened its alert levels to the maximum. Red lines appear to be US military presence/actions in the region, Iranian attacks on commercial shipping/US personnel, and Iran's nuclear program advancement.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **United States** has conducted multiple waves of strikes in Iran and issued a "global alert" for its citizens in the Middle East. President Trump stated that Iran would "pay many times over" for any American soldier deaths and assured that Israeli PM Netanyahu would not be arrested in the US. The US Energy Secretary affirmed commitment to ensuring oil flow through Hormuz, with or without Iran's cooperation. US intelligence assessments, however, suggest that current strikes are not effectively influencing Iran's leadership, leading to an "undefined interim state" between peace and war. The US is also imposing a 50% tariff on Canadian products.

**Gulf States** are directly impacted, with Kuwait and Bahrain actively intercepting Iranian attacks. Saudi Arabia condemned the Houthi maritime blockade. Qatari mediators have been involved in proposing a 10-day ceasefire. Qatar also reported Iranian attacks on a Qatari tanker and a missile attack on its territory to the UN. The GCC, including Oman, issued a joint statement accusing Iran of "war crimes" in Kuwait and Bahrain.

Among **EU members**, France's Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot warned of "consequences" following the detention and assault of two French embassy staff in Tehran. Air France has suspended flights to Saudi Arabia and the UAE. The **United Kingdom's** new Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, discussed mine clearing in the Strait of Hormuz with President Trump.

**Russia** is seeing an upcoming visit from FBI Director Kash Patel in October, the first since 2013, amidst reports of Russia expelling two Italian diplomats. The **UN** may see a significant change as the Trump administration is considering cutting ties with the UNHCR, while Iran has urged the UN Security Council to condemn US attacks on its nuclear facilities. The **Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)** expressed deep concern over the escalating Middle East situation, warning against actions that could undermine diplomatic efforts.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Several contradictions and unverified claims are present in the raw intelligence feed. Iranian sources contradicted each other on a potential 10-day ceasefire proposal: the Foreign Ministry initially denied it, while a senior Iranian official later confirmed mediators had proposed it and it was under examination. Similarly, the Governor of Isfahan denied a US attack in the city despite multiple reports of explosions, indicating potential confusion or deliberate obfuscation. US and Iranian reports on casualties in Jordan diverge significantly, with the Pentagon confirming injuries but not deaths beyond the initial two, while Iranian sources claim "several" killed and accuse the US of concealing numbers.

Unverified claims include Omiddana's report of Iran's 65th Army Brigade movement towards Abadan for potential operations in Bubiyan Island, Kuwait, and KianMeli's claim of a Saudi tanker being hit by an Iranian missile in Hormuz. Omiddana also reported confirmed explosions in Baneh without further detail. KianMeli's claim that "attacks on Iran on a large scale are imminent, Tehran soon" appears sensationalized. Reports of widespread internet blackouts in Iran and the nature of a "Chinese air defense system" in Bahrain lack independent verification.

Propaganda indicators are evident in both US and Iranian messaging. Iranian state media consistently uses terms like "child-killing army" and "Great Satan" for the US. The IRGC's emphasis on "clearing radar and air-defense systems" frames their actions as successful and preparatory. US statements focus on protecting commercial shipping and holding Iran accountable. Smotrich's comment on the "current situation" being best for Israel might be aimed at shaping public opinion.

Reporting gaps include precise details on the scale of damage from US strikes in Iran, independent verification of specific US casualty numbers from Iranian attacks, and the full scope of the proposed 10-day ceasefire deal.
